items.title: A requested noun with ください
items.explanation: Please give me the named item, optionally with the already taught item count. This noun request precedes later verb てください teaching.

items.title: Own-family and polite family terms
items.pattern: 父/母 versus お父さん/お母さん
items.explanation: Own-family outside descriptions commonly use 父/母; polite/familiar terms depend on whom one describes or addresses. They are whole words, not universal replacements.

items.title: Politely ask a name
items.explanation: お marks respect for the person's name in the question. The supplied answer uses 名前はゆきです or 私はゆきです; fit the question to an appropriate introduction context.

items.title: Language as the spoken object
items.pattern: 日本語 を 話します
items.explanation: を marks the spoken language in this model. Distinguish a conversation partner と and language as medium で.

items.title: Language or channel as a medium
items.pattern: 日本語/電話 で 話します
items.explanation: で gives the language used or the phone as means/channel. 日本語を話します is another natural relationship, not an incorrect alternative.

items.title: と after the exact quoted words
items.explanation: と marks the quote; に can identify the person addressed. Distinguish quoted words from companion と and noun-list と. Broader plain-form reported statements come later.

items.title: 全然 with a negative
items.explanation: The taught beginner pattern means not at all. 話しません describes non-use/habit in the supplied context, not inability.

items.title: Greetings ending in written は
items.pattern: こんにちは / こんばんは
items.explanation: The fixed greetings end in written は, pronounced わ. Use them as whole basic expressions with the taught social context.
